newsitem.title: USA: US West unit debt deal upped to $4.1 bln -Merrill.
newsitem.headline: US West unit debt deal upped to $4.1 bln -Merrill.

text.p: US West unit U.S. West Capital Funding's multi-tranche debt offering was increased in size for the third time to $4.1 billion on Thursday, according to lead manager Merrill Lynch & Co.

According to the lead underwriter, the debt offering when priced would hold the record for the largest investment grade debt offering ever, pushing Lockheed Martin Corp's $3.5 billion 1996 debt deal into second place.

Growing demand for US West Capital's deal triggered the issuer to lift the size of the offering from its initially planned sale of $2.0 billion to $2.25 billion on Tuesday, and again to $3.5 billion on Wednesday, dealers said.
"There's just been huge demand for the deal," said one high-grade syndicate source.
Investors craved more and the deal was increased to $4.1 billion and a sixth tranche was added, syndicate sources said.
The sixth tranche includes a $200 million 35-year bond with price talk seen at 132 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, dealers said.
The current breakdown on the additional five tranches is as follows, syndicate sources said on Thursday.
-$600 million in five-year notes, upped from $500 million, with price talk seen at between 55 to 58 basis points over Treasuries.
-$1.1 billion in 10-year debt, upped from $1.0 billion, with price talk seen between 80 to 83 basis points over Treasuries.
-$1.1 billion in 30-year bonds, upped from $1.0 billion, with price talk at 107-110 basis points over Treasuries.
-$600 million in 40-year bonds, upped from $500 million, puttable in seventh year, with price talk between 56 to 58 basis points over Treasuries.
-$500 million in 100-year bonds with price talk seen between 120 and 123 basis points.
The Baa1/BBB-plus deal is expected to be priced early Thursday afternoon, dealers said.
